nodes.summary: For an assignment $v$ of Boolean values to the variables $0, 1, 2, \ldots$ and a clause $C$, whose literals are pairs $(x, b)$ of a variable $x$ and a polarity $b$, this Boolean is true exactly when some literal $(x, b)$ of $C$ satisfies $v(x) = b$.
nodes.title: Boolean clause satisfaction check

nodes.summary: Given a natural number $n$ (the fuel) and a CNF formula $\varphi$, the procedure returns a Boolean value. Literals are pairs $(x, b)$ of a variable $x$ and a polarity $b$. With fuel $0$ the procedure returns true exactly when $\varphi$ has no clauses. With fuel $n + 1$ it returns true if $\varphi$ has no clauses, and otherwise returns false if some clause of $\varphi$ is empty. Otherwise, if some clause of…
nodes.title: DPLL with a fuel budget

nodes.summary: On a CNF formula $\varphi$, the DPLL procedure runs DPLL with fuel equal to the number of distinct variables occurring in $\varphi$ and returns its Boolean result.
nodes.title: The DPLL procedure

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, read as a list of clauses, this returns the literal $\ell$ of the first clause of $\varphi$ that consists of the single literal $\ell$, and returns nothing when no clause of $\varphi$ has exactly one literal.
nodes.title: First unit literal

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, read as a list of clauses, this returns the variable of the first literal of the first nonempty clause of $\varphi$, that is, the first variable occurring in $\varphi$ in source order, and returns nothing when every clause of $\varphi$ is empty (in particular when $\varphi$ has no clauses).
nodes.title: First variable of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: For an assignment $v$ of Boolean values to the variables $0, 1, 2, \ldots$ and a CNF formula $\varphi$, this Boolean is true exactly when every clause of $\varphi$ passes the Boolean clause satisfaction check for $v$, that is, every clause contains a literal $(x, b)$ with $v(x) = b$.
nodes.title: Boolean formula satisfaction check

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
